newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were sharply lower on Tuesday morning, with profit-taking pushing down the Hang Seng Index by 152 points, or 1.06 percent, to 14,286 in early trade, brokers said.
Profit-taking was seen on property stocks, utilities and China-related stocks, brokers said.
"Rumours and bad news on properties, red chips and H-shares expedited the pace of the price fall," said Peter Lui, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
Lui said the market was hit by possible government measures to cool speculation in the property market and Beijing's recent drive to curb speculative trading in China's stock markets.
News that senior officials at H-share company Guangshen Railway had been relieved of duties over allegations of improper investments also dampened sentiment, he said.
The blue-chip index regained some ground by mid-morning to 14,299, down 140 points, or 0.97 percent, after touching a low of 14,213.95.

"The market should find good support at 14,200," said a chartist with a local house. "We should see a technical rebound off that level today or tomorrow. If not, we could see weakness in the Hang Seng in the next two weeks."
Hongkong Telecom lost HK$0.75 to HK$16.60, Cheung Kong was down HK$1.25 at HK$73.75 and Henderson Land fell HK$2.25 to HK$67.25.
